blocks.text: Dohra:

As (imprisoned) Banda Singh reached Narela1 (an outskirt of Delhi), Emperor (Farrukhsiar) felt extremely threatened in his heart. He was wary of Banda Singh's entry into the city of Delhi, As Banda Singh was reported to be a very dangerous person. (1)
lines: As (imprisoned) Banda Singh reached Narela1 (an outskirt of Delhi),
Emperor (Farrukhsiar) felt extremely threatened in his heart.
He was wary of Banda Singh's entry into the city of Delhi,
As Banda Singh was reported to be a very dangerous person.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

As the Emperor himself put his lodgings across the river Yamuna, He kept Banda Singh imprisoned on this side of the river. After gouging out Banda Singh's eyes and blinding him, Banda Singh was made to move ahead of Narela town. (2)
lines: As the Emperor himself put his lodgings across the river Yamuna,
He kept Banda Singh imprisoned on this side of the river.
After gouging out Banda Singh's eyes and blinding him,
Banda Singh was made to move ahead of Narela town.

blocks.text: Emperor Farukhsiar resolved it in his own mind, That peace will not prevail without beheading Banda Singh. The emperor sent his designated messengers to Banda Singh, Who asked Banda Singh to eat his favourite food before death. (3)
lines: Emperor Farukhsiar resolved it in his own mind,
That peace will not prevail without beheading Banda Singh.
The emperor sent his designated messengers to Banda Singh,
Who asked Banda Singh to eat his favourite food before death.

blocks.text: Banda Singh was asked to get ready to face death, And asked to choose the manner of his death as well. Then Banda Singh answered their enquiries in this manner: That he would be killed in the manner the emperor himself wished to die. (4)
lines: Banda Singh was asked to get ready to face death,
And asked to choose the manner of his death as well.
Then Banda Singh answered their enquiries in this manner: That he would be killed in the manner the emperor himself wished to die.

blocks.text: After this reply, Banda Singh took a vow of silence, While the royal messengers conveyed Banda Singh's message. The emperor heard whatever Banda Singh had conveyed, And (dear reader) listen further how death dealt with both of them. (5)
lines: After this reply,
Banda Singh took a vow of silence,
While the royal messengers conveyed Banda Singh's message.
The emperor heard whatever Banda Singh had conveyed,
And (dear reader) listen further how death dealt with both of them.

blocks.text: Dohra:
The Emperor Farrukhsiar kept Banda Singh in custody for many days, After the gouging of his eyes and rendering him blind.
(Dear readers) listen further as I have discovered, How both Banda Singh and Farukhsiar died one after the other. (6)
lines: (Dear readers) listen further as I have discovered,
How both Banda Singh and Farukhsiar died one after the other.

blocks.text: There was one Kazi (Islamic scholar) in Farukhsiar's court, Who was the real brother of (Wazir Khan) the Nawab of Sirhind. Banda Singh had beheaded Wazir Khan (after capture of Sirhind), After dragging his body after tying it to a pair of oxens. (7)
lines: There was one Kazi (Islamic scholar) in Farukhsiar's court,
Who was the real brother of (Wazir Khan) the Nawab of Sirhind.
Banda Singh had beheaded Wazir Khan (after capture of Sirhind),
After dragging his body after tying it to a pair of oxens.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

This Qazi misguided and advised Farrukhsiar (out of malice), That the emperor would have to regret if he spared Banda Singh's life. There were so may other Singhs alive of the calibre of Banda Singh, Whom Banda Singh had empowered (in his own lifetime). (8)
lines: This Qazi misguided and advised Farrukhsiar (out of malice),
That the emperor would have to regret if he spared Banda Singh's life.
There were so may other Singhs alive of the calibre of Banda Singh,
Whom Banda Singh had empowered (in his own lifetime).

blocks.text: He had imparted to many of them the miraculous art of flying, And many of his sons were also still alive as well. All of these followers and sons would feel emboldened if he survived, But they would disappear in case he was eliminated. (9)
lines: He had imparted to many of them the miraculous art of flying,
And many of his sons were also still alive as well.
All of these followers and sons would feel emboldened if he survived,
But they would disappear in case he was eliminated.

blocks.text: As there being a surfeit of those who advocated Banda Singh's elimination, They gave a very exaggerated account about Banda Singh's powers. (So) Farrukhsiar calling a conclave of Islamic scholars, Made them issue Islamic (decrees) against Banda Singh. (10)
lines: As there being a surfeit of those who advocated Banda Singh's elimination,
They gave a very exaggerated account about Banda Singh's powers.
(So) Farrukhsiar calling a conclave of Islamic scholars,
Made them issue Islamic (decrees) against Banda Singh.

blocks.text: They recommended the adoption of a policy of revenge, And dragging of Banda Singh's body as he had done unto Wazir Khan. Recommending Banda Singh's body to be tied behind a horse. They wished it to be dragged around the city of Delhi. (11)
lines: They recommended the adoption of a policy of revenge,
And dragging of Banda Singh's body as he had done unto Wazir Khan.
Recommending Banda Singh's body to be tied behind a horse.
They wished it to be dragged around the city of Delhi.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Banda Singh's dead body should be dumped and abandoned, After being dragged and paraded through the city. A message would go that those who indulged in anti-state activities, Would meet the same fate as was meted out to Banda Singh. (12)
lines: Banda Singh's dead body should be dumped and abandoned,
After being dragged and paraded through the city.
A message would go that those who indulged in anti-state activities,
Would meet the same fate as was meted out to Banda Singh.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Implementing whatever had been recommended by the Islamic scholars, The emperor ordered the dragging of Banda Singh's body behind a horse. (Thus) sending a message that those who indulged in such activities, Would meet the same fate as was meted out to Bnada Singh. (13)
lines: Implementing whatever had been recommended by the Islamic scholars,
The emperor ordered the dragging of Banda Singh's body behind a horse.
(Thus) sending a message that those who indulged in such activities,
Would meet the same fate as was meted out to Bnada Singh.

blocks.text: So was Banda Singh executed and done to death in this manner, I (the author) have got it recorded as I have heard it (from my sources). Some people remarked that Banda Singh had not died, Since no trace of his funeral pile was traced, he must have flown away. (14)
lines: So was Banda Singh executed and done to death in this manner,
I (the author) have got it recorded as I have heard it (from my sources).
Some people remarked that Banda Singh had not died,
Since no trace of his funeral pile was traced, he must have flown away.

blocks.text: However, the author did not buy such an argument, Because Banda Singh must have emerged had he been alive. All the other Singhs were executed after Banda Singh's execution, After beating, dragging and dishonouring their dead bodies. (15)
lines: However, the author did not buy such an argument,
Because Banda Singh must have emerged had he been alive.
All the other Singhs were executed after Banda Singh's execution,
After beating, dragging and dishonouring their dead bodies.

blocks.text: S. Baaj Singh, proving true to his salt and oath of allegiance, Sacrificed his life along with three of his brothers. The two brothers Aali Singh and (Maali Singh) of village Salodi, Also sacrificed their lives along with Banda Singh. (16)
lines: S.
Baaj Singh, proving true to his salt and oath of allegiance,
Sacrificed his life along with three of his brothers.
The two brothers Aali Singh and (Maali Singh) of village Salodi,
Also sacrificed their lives along with Banda Singh.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Whatever Rattan Singh (the author of this epic) had heard (about Banda Singh) He has narrated it ad verbatim (to his readers). It was in the year of Seventeen hundred seventy eight2 , That Banda Singh shed his mortal frame. (17)
lines: Whatever Rattan Singh (the author of this epic) had heard (about Banda Singh) He has narrated it ad verbatim (to his readers).
It was in the year of Seventeen hundred seventy eight2 ,
That Banda Singh shed his mortal frame.
